picks.rationale: MPC is up +117% YTD and +19% in the last month, with a P/E of 12.3 and a 1.1% dividend yield. Refining margins are surging due to Middle East supply disruptions, and the stock has strong momentum and positive news sentiment (+0.25).

Valero is up +150% over the past year and +110% YTD, with a P/E of 14.2 and a 1.4% dividend yield. Record refining profits are being driven by high crack spreads, and the stock has strong momentum and a positive analyst consensus.

Equinor is up +72% YTD and +15% in the last month, with a P/E of 11.1 and a 3.8% dividend yield. The stock benefits from high oil prices and strong European gas demand, though analyst consensus is hold (3.33) and short interest is elevated at 2.95%.

ConocoPhillips is up +33% YTD and +14% in the last month, with a P/E of 16.8 and a 2.7% dividend yield. The company has a strong analyst score (1.64) and positive news sentiment (+0.20), and is well-positioned for high oil prices.

SLB is up +35% YTD and +13% in the last month, with a P/E of 26.2 and a 2.2% dividend yield. The stock has the best analyst score (1.6) and highest news sentiment (+0.33) in the universe, driven by strong oilfield services demand.

Baker Hughes is up +39% YTD and +14% in the last month, with a P/E of 20.8 and a 1.4% dividend yield. The stock has strong momentum, a positive analyst score (1.71), and benefits from rising rig counts and LNG demand.

Exxon is up +32% YTD and +11% in the last month, with a P/E of 20.6 and a 2.6% dividend yield. Despite a slight EPS miss, the company posted record production and strong cash flows, and is trading at a premium valuation but with solid fundamentals.

Chevron is up +31% YTD and +10% in the last month, with a P/E of 19.2 and a 3.6% dividend yield. The company beat Q2 EPS estimates and has a strong analyst score (1.72), with positive news sentiment (+0.28).

TotalEnergies is up +34% YTD and +10% in the last month, with a P/E of 11.1 and a 4.8% dividend yield. The stock offers a high dividend yield and benefits from high oil prices, though analyst coverage is limited.

Occidental is up +39% YTD and +9% in the last month, with a P/E of 17.2 and a 1.9% dividend yield. The company has a strong analyst score (2.33) and is benefiting from high oil prices and debt reduction, though short interest is very low.
